title: The boundary is substitutable via the framework interface so tests exercise it without booting the whole stack
asA: test author verifying that a specific exception produces the expected record
iWant: the boundary contract to expose a substitutable interface so a test can exercise the error-handling path without booting the full framework
soThat: boundary tests are hermetic and fast

acceptanceCriteria.description: TAC-1701 exposes a boundaryFor({ loggerFactory, transportWriter }) -> { handle(err, context) } function the framework registers as its handler; a test constructs the boundary with a stub loggerFactory and a stub transportWriter, invokes handle(err, context), and asserts the observed loggerFactory calls and the observed transportWriter calls.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a stub loggerFactory and a stub transportWriter
acceptanceCriteria.when: the test invokes handle with a synthetic exception
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stub loggerFactory records one error() call with the constructed record and the stub transportWriter records one write with the mapped wire body

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given `boundaryFor({ loggerFactory: null, transportWriter: <stub> })` called with a null or undefined loggerFactory, the constructor refuses with a controlled error naming the missing dependency; no partial boundary is returned. Symmetric refusal for `boundaryFor({ loggerFactory: <stub>, transportWriter: null })`. The check enumerates the two null-injection shapes and inspects the thrown error.
acceptanceCriteria.given: boundaryFor called with a null or undefined loggerFactory or transportWriter
acceptanceCriteria.then: it throws a controlled error naming the missing dependency; no partial boundary is returned

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a constructed boundary with a stub loggerFactory, when `boundary.handle(err, context)` is called with a synthetic error, then the stub loggerFactory's `error()` receives exactly one call whose first argument is the constructed record (record.code, record.category, record.correlationId present), the stub transportWriter receives exactly one call carrying the same record, and no direct process.stderr.write fires during the call.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a boundary constructed with stub loggerFactory and transportWriter, invoked on a synthetic error
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stubs each receive exactly one call carrying the constructed record; no process.stderr.write fires during the call

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a constructed boundary, when `boundary.handle(err, context)` is called and the stub transportWriter throws, then the boundary contract catches the transport failure, emits one additional record through the stub loggerFactory naming the transport failure, and does not re-throw; the caller (the framework) sees a clean return.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a boundary whose stub transportWriter throws when called
acceptanceCriteria.then: the boundary catches the transport throw, emits one additional record through the loggerFactory naming the transport failure, and returns cleanly to the caller
